key_insight: PING combines graph neural networks with advection–diffusion physics to forecast transport dynamics on irregular sensor networks and support solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: More accurate intra-day photovoltaic power forecasts can help grid operators integrate variable solar generation.
method: Represent transported particle concentrations as signals on an irregular graph.
Add a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models using ground-based measurements and satellite cloud information.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, and improved intra-day PV forecasting through hybrid modeling.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical gains or deployment costs, and a soft physics constraint does not guarantee physical consistency.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
